🏛️ Virtue Spotlight — Courtesy
Curators study other people's places. When we name countries, we take care to spell them right and say them carefully. Courtesy means treating every place we study — and the people who live there — with respect.

🔍 TEACHING · EXPLORE
Four Places, One Region
🎬
Teacher recording notes: Use a real map of North America. Point out: Canada is the country to the north — it stretches all the way to the Arctic. The United States sits in the middle, between Canada and Mexico. Mexico is south of the United States. The Caribbean is the group of islands in a warm sea, south of Florida and east of Mexico. Show the four labels on the map one at a time. Then walk through the flip cards and how to place labels on the map activity below. 3–5 minutes.
1
Learn the Story
📖
Four Places, One Region
Meet the countries of North America and the Caribbean

The world is huge. To study it, geographers look at one region at a time. A region is a group of places that have something in common — they're close together, share borders, or are connected by oceans, history, or culture.

Today's region has four parts:

⬆️ Canada sits in the far north. It reaches all the way up to the Arctic and is the second-largest country on Earth.

↕️ The United States sits in the middle, sharing a long border with Canada to the north and Mexico to the south. It stretches from the Atlantic Ocean to the Pacific Ocean.

⬇️ Mexico sits south of the United States. Its land gets narrower as it goes south, toward Central America.

↘️ The Caribbean is not one country — it's a group of islands in a warm sea, south of Florida and east of Mexico. Cuba, Jamaica, Haiti, the Dominican Republic, and Puerto Rico are some of the places in the Caribbean. Puerto Rico is part of the United States. It is a U.S. territory.

All four sit close together on the map. That's why curators group them as one region.

🤔

Pause & Think: The Caribbean is mostly water and islands, while Canada is one huge country. Why might curators still group them together with the United States and Mexico?

🔤 Word Root: -ern

-ern means toward or in the direction of. Add it to a direction word: north → northern, south → southern, east → eastern, west → western.

Try it: Canada is in the northern part of our region. Mexico is in the southern part.

United States
The country in the middle. It borders Canada to the north and Mexico to the south, and reaches both the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. Its capital is Washington, D.C.

Mexico
The country south of the United States. It narrows toward Central America and touches both the Pacific Ocean and the Gulf of Mexico. Its capital is Mexico City.

Place the Labels
Match each country label to the right clue.

Read each clue and tap the country that matches it. Get all four right to finish the map.

Clue 1: "I'm the country in the far north. I'm the second-largest country on Earth and I reach all the way to the Arctic."
Clue 2: "I sit in the middle, between Canada and Mexico. I touch both the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans."
Clue 3: "I sit south of the United States. My land gets narrower as it goes south, toward Central America. My capital is Mexico City."
Clue 4: "We're not one country — we're a chain of islands in a warm sea. Cuba, Jamaica, and Puerto Rico are part of us."
🎉 All four labels placed!
🔎 Discovery Fact: The Caribbean Sea has more than 7,000 islands, big and small. They make up 13 independent countries, plus many places that belong to other countries, like Puerto Rico.
⏳

Then & Now: In the past, the borders between these countries looked very different — Mexico once reached much farther north than it does now. Today, the borders we see on the map have been the same for a long time. What stayed the same? People still live close together in this region and trade across borders every day.

4
Connect the Ideas
🏷️ Exhibit Label

North America and the Caribbean is one region with four major parts: Canada in the north, the United States in the middle, Mexico to the south, and the Caribbean islands to the southeast. They are studied together because they share the same part of the world.

🦉
🧭 Opti says…
Quick curator tip: "America" is not the name of one country. The Americas means North America and South America together. That's why careful curators say "the United States" when they mean just one country.

You've placed the labels. Let's see how well you know where each one belongs.

🧠
Quick Self-Check
🧠

Not graded — just for you! Answer these three questions to see how much you remember before writing your evidence responses.

1. Which country sits in the middle, between Canada and Mexico?
ACuba
BThe United States
CCanada
Right! The United States borders Canada to the north and Mexico to the south.
Picture the map: Canada is on top, Mexico is on the bottom. Which country sits between them?
2. Which of these is part of the Caribbean?
AMexico City
BOttawa
CCuba
Yes! Cuba is one of the Caribbean islands, along with Jamaica, Haiti, the Dominican Republic, and Puerto Rico.
The Caribbean is a group of islands. Which choice is an island in a warm sea — not a capital city of a big country?
3. Why do curators study these four places as one region?
AThey sit close together in the same part of the world.
BThey all speak the same language.
CThey are all the exact same size.
Exactly! A region is a group of places that share something — and these four share the same part of the world. They are neighbors.
Think about what makes a region. Is it about size, language, or being close together on the map?

Evidence Questions

B
Curator Task: Gallery Introduction
Write the introduction visitors read when they step into the new gallery.

The North America & Caribbean Gallery needs an introduction. Tell visitors where each place is, compared to the place next to it. Link all four in one direction sentence, like a chain: Canada is ___ of the United States, which is ___ of Mexico, which is ___ of the Caribbean. Then add one sentence of your own: why do these four places make one region, or what makes the Caribbean different?

Your introduction should: name all four places · use a direction word to link each place to the next one · add one sentence of your own.
